clue.text: Old suit — Egyptian — to look at in the British Museum

indicators.note: in places the Egyptian and looking pieces inside the museum's initials

parts.note: BM is the standard abbreviation for the British Museum
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian
to see is to look at

explanation.surface: Someone admires an ancient Egyptian costume on display at the British Museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is a verb here, in its archaic sense of being fitting or becoming; the old-fashioned answer is flagged by 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to befit or be proper for, which is what suiting someone means.

clue.text: Dodge of old king maybe centred in the Orient

indicators.note: centred in puts the king's name in the middle, flanked by the eastern letters

parts.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E, here taken on both sides of the king
Lud is a legendary early king of Britain, said to have given his name to Ludgate in London

explanation.surface: A trick played by some ancient monarch with his heart in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: KING LUD is a legendary pre-Roman king of Britain; 'maybe' marks him as one example of an old king. The East letter E is placed on each side of him.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to evade or escape it neatly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Surpasses — with one gold, is higher

parts.note: excels means surpasses or outdoes
I is the Roman numeral one
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: An athlete outdoes the rest and, wearing a gold medal, stands on the top step.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Latin, used as a motto meaning 'ever upward'; OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin comparative meaning loftier or still upward, famous as the New York state motto.

clue.text: Some agree only some: unsatisfying

indicators.note: only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: When only a few people agree, the outcome feels thin and disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scanty or skimpy portion leaves one wanting more, so it fails to satisfy.

clue.text: Make up to stuffy person after impudence

indicators.note: after puts the stuffy person behind the impudence in the answer

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, impudence
an old stick is a dull, stuffy person

explanation.surface: Someone sucks up to a pompous bore after being cheeky to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up to' reads as flatter or ingratiate oneself, but 'Make up' is a noun, cosmetics; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured cosmetic for the lips is one of the commonest kinds of facial cosmetics.

clue.text: Elemental danger that may affect industry

explanation.surface: A natural hazard that can bring factories to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a sudden walkout by workers with no notice, which hits industry without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt from a thunderstorm is a danger from the elements, while a sudden unannounced walkout by workers disrupts industry.

clue.text: Old Turkish Sultan's ship had a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Ottoman ruler's vessel was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a disaster' rearranges SHIP HAD A; the 's after 'Sultan' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian-derived title for a great king, used of the Ottoman emperor.

clue.text: Shark runs the boozer

parts.note: a tope is a small shark
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A predatory man operates the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' is British slang for a pub, but here it means a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual heavy drinker, an old-fashioned word for a drunkard.

clue.text: Deals competently with sound finishing touch

parts.note: copes means manages or deals competently
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: Someone handles a sound system well and adds a final flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: The top stone of a wall or building, figuratively the crowning final element of a work.

clue.text: Stung — rush in voiceless

indicators.note: in places the rushing piece inside the voiceless one

parts.note: surd is a phonetic term for a voiceless consonant
to charge is to rush forward

explanation.surface: A stung animal charges about in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stung' means overcharged, as when a customer is fleeced; SURD is the phonetics term for voiceless.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stung is slang for being overcharged, which is having an extra levy added.

clue.text: Objectionable young chap with a torpid insect

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky, conceited young man

explanation.surface: An unpleasant youth keeps a sluggish bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The inactive stage of an insect between larva and adult, when it lies dormant in a case.

clue.text: Red wine, including the Spanish, in the sideboard

indicators.note: including means the wine word holds the Spanish article within it

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Red wine, Spanish included, is kept in the dining-room cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet or sideboard for keeping wine bottles in a dining room.

clue.text: Most touchy in this way — take it easy

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
to rest is to take it easy

explanation.surface: Advice to the most irritable person: calm down like this.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sore in its sense of aggrieved or irritable, so most touchy.

clue.text: I charge ahead in motorized charger

indicators.note: ahead puts the charge in front of the letter I

parts.note: a tax is a charge

explanation.surface: A knight on a mechanical horse leads the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charger' looks like a warhorse, but a cab is motorized and charges a fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab with a meter is a vehicle that charges for each journey.

clue.text: Vary one old choice food and have a row

parts.note: to alter is to vary
cates is an archaic word for delicacies; one of them is a cate

explanation.surface: Change a dish of old delicacies and start a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: CATES, an archaic plural, were dainties; 'one' points to the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or quarrel angrily with someone, the verb behind the noun for a heated argument.

clue.text: Vegetation, indeed

explanation.surface: Plant life, really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vegetation' means vegetating, idleness; 'indeed' read as 'in deed' means in action, the answer split.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetating means idleness, doing nothing; 'in deed' cryptically means in action, i.e. through actual doing.

clue.text: Religious madness in the Gulf; state

parts.note: taken as written
Oman is a Gulf state
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: Religious fanaticism flourishes in a Gulf country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulf state' looks like one phrase naming a single country, but it splits: the Gulf country, then a US state by its postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: A delusion that one is a god, or a religious obsession, from Greek theos god plus mania.

clue.text: When one day seems just like the next

definitions.text: When one day seems just like the next

parts.words: When one day seems just like the next
parts.note: reads as a dull routine, but is the exact moment one day turns into the following one

explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night is the instant when the date changes over, so the end of one day is the start of the next.

clue.text: Jack gets in sweetened drink for a bird

indicators.note: gets in means the sailor goes inside the drink

parts.note: a sling is a sweetened spirit drink, as in Singapore sling
jack is slang for a sailor, as is tar

explanation.surface: A sailor orders a sweet cocktail for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' also suggests British slang for a young woman, but it is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A common speckled songbird of the genus Sturnus.

clue.text: She came second, with small new flat wanted

parts.note: Eve was created after Adam, the second human
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A woman who finished runner-up wants a small new apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: EVE came second in Genesis, after Adam; 'flat' is not a home but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Level or smooth, without bumps.

clue.text: A short spell in Society informally, of course

parts.note: natch is slang short for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A brief stint in high society is, naturally, expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief period or fragment of activity, as in a snatch of sleep.

clue.text: For a start, there's nothing to dress in

parts.note: O is the zero, nothing
to rig out is to dress

explanation.surface: To begin with, nobody has anything to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: The point where something begins, its beginning or source.

clue.text: Drink up on direction? Stuff!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the drink is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: grog is a drink of rum and water
E is the compass direction east

explanation.surface: A drinker downs one on instruction and exclaims in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the drink, as a down clue reads upwards; 'on' places the direction after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself greedily with food.

clue.text: He works with metal — a money maker?

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a smith is a maker, a craftsman

explanation.surface: A metalworker is a moneymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and repairs things in thin sheet metal, a whitesmith.

clue.text: A way in and up in Latin, in a sense

indicators.note: in places the article and the street inside the Latin conjunction
up in a down clue means the Latin word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: et is the Latin for and, as the clue's in Latin says
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A path leads in, then upwards in Latin, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Latin' tells you to translate 'and'; 'up' reverses that Latin word in this down clue, and 'in' sets A and the way inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five senses, the one using the tongue.

clue.text: Just as remote about one

indicators.note: about means the remote word goes around the numeral

parts.note: far means remote, distant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Equally distant, roughly one.
explanation.walkthrough: FAR round I gives FAIR, meaning just; the grid's PAIR has no parse here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair dealing is impartial and equitable, the same as just.

clue.text: Sets tiring fashion: strength of character needed

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Setting exhausting trends calls for real backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, so having it means determination and pluck.

clue.text: Writer in a snare — he needs a drug of forgetfulness

indicators.note: in places the writer inside the snare

parts.note: a net is a snare
a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: An author caught in a trap needs something to help him forget.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend, a potion that banished grief and memory, as in Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Led to give careful attention about a daughter

indicators.note: about means the attention word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to heed is to pay careful attention

explanation.surface: The leader took care to watch over a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To head something is to lead it, so the past tense means led.
